title: The projective-line adjunction for towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an arbitrary scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and their ordinary derived category [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. For a scheme $T$ over $S$, write $\mathscr C^+(T)$ for the full subcategory of $D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ whose level $n$, for every $n\geq1$, is in the essential image of $\nu_T^*:D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)\to D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)$; this means there exists an etale-origin witness as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Write $\mathbf P^1_T=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};T)$ as in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $\Delta:\mathbf P^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the diagonal.

Let $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, and let $p_1,p_2:\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S\to\mathbf P^1_S$
be the projections. Define, for $K_\bullet\in\mathscr C^+(S)$ and
$M_\bullet\in\mathscr C^+(\mathbf P^1_S)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet):\ &Rq_{*,\bullet}(q_\bullet^*K_\bullet(1)[2])
\simeq K_\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_{*,\bullet}(\mathcal O_{E,\mathbf P^1_S}/\ell^\bullet)(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{id}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}\ }K_\bullet,\\
\eta_\bullet(M_\bullet):\ &M_\bullet\simeq Rp_{2*,\bullet}\Delta_*M_\bullet
\xrightarrow{\ Rp_{2*,\bullet}(\delta_\bullet\otimes p_1^*M_\bullet)\ }
Rp_{2*,\bullet}p_1^*M_\bullet(1)[2]\simeq q_\bullet^*Rq_{*,\bullet}M_\bullet(1)[2],
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}$ and $\delta_\bullet$ from [det-sp-tower-classes].
Then $\eta_\bullet$ and $\varepsilon_\bullet$ are the unit and counit of an
adjunction $Rq_{*,\bullet}\dashv q_\bullet^*(-)(1)[2]$ between $\mathscr C^+(\mathbf P^1_S)$ and $\mathscr C^+(S)$, whose
evaluation at level $n$ is the finite projective-line adjunction. In particular this adjunction restricts to the full subcategories of uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers].

proof.text: *Domains and natural maps.* Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $W=P\times_SP$, $A_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^\bullet$, $F=Rq_{*,\bullet}$ and $G=q^*_\bullet(-)(1)[2]$. The bounded-below level computation [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels] applies to $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$; the comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] for these quasi-compact quasi-separated maps shows that their direct images preserve etale-origin levels. The finite etale twist is locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], with $N=\ell^n$ and $A=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Inverse image and this twist preserve these levels, so $F,G$ have the asserted domains. Each of $q,p_1,p_2$ is a projective-line projection, hence proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. The diagonal is the closed Cartier divisor in [det-sp-tower-classes], hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). Its complementary open is quasi-compact: on an affine, cover by finitely many principal opens trivializing its invertible ideal; the complement in each is one further principal open. By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], $\Delta_*$ is exact at every finite level, hence exact on towers since exactness is levelwise. Thus $R\Delta_{*,\bullet}=\Delta_*$, justifying the notation in the unit formula. For these proper maps use the compactification with open part the identity in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Its projection formula identifies $\Delta_*M$ with $\Delta_*A_P\otimes^L p_1^*M$ since $\Delta^*p_1^*M=M$, and its proper exchange identifies $Rp_{2*,\bullet}p_1^*M$ with $q^*_\bullet FM$. These give exactly the displayed natural $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$. The simultaneous tensor, composition and adjunction models in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], applied to $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, ensure that these are actual tower maps with the indicated evaluations. Write $t_i=\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i,\bullet}$. Under proper exchange $t_i$ is the base change of $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}$: the two components of the splitting [det-sp-tower-classes] are the unit and the Kummer boundary of $\mathcal O(1)$; inverse image preserves the unit, pulls back $\mathcal O(1)$, and commutes with the boundary of the pulled-back short exact Kummer sequence. Thus exchange identifies the splitting maps themselves, their inverses, and their second projections.

proof.text: *The two scalar endomorphisms and detection.* Let $\alpha_i:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{i*,\bullet}\Delta_*A_P$ be the composition identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$, and put $c_i=t_i\circ Rp_{i*,\bullet}(\delta_\bullet)\circ\alpha_i$. These are endomorphisms of $A_P[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to the abelian tower category of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]: each $c_i$ is a unique compatible family of module-sheaf maps. If all evaluated $c_i$ are identities, their underlying families equal the identity family, so $c_i=1$. This uses equality detection only between these degree-zero objects. The composition identification is the canonical derived-direct-image comparison supplied on tower section models by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

*Finite diagonal integrals over arbitrary bases.* Fix $n\geq1$, set $N=\ell^n$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. This is a finite commutative ring killed by $N$, and $N$ is invertible on $S$. Exact evaluation and the canonical direct-image comparison identify the level maps with the ordinary etale constructions below: [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] provide the evaluations and actual comparison maps; [det-sp-tower-classes] identifies the classes and splitting. The comparison $\nu^*$ is fully faithful on $D^+$ by [sk-prop-sf-comparison], so an equality proved for these etale maps gives the equality for their pro-etale images.

For any scheme $T$ over $S$, let $r:P_T=\mathbf P^1_T\to T$, and let $b_T:B_T(1)[2]\oplus B_T\to Rr_*B_{P_T}(1)[2]$ have components the shifted twisted unit and the scalar-extended Kummer class $h_T=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. The Kummer construction is valid on arbitrary $T$ by [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Apply [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] to $r$ and any geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. It has no Noetherian or finite-type-over-a-field hypothesis on $T$. The projective-space pullback identity [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] identifies the fibre with $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. The twist pullback isomorphism [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], naturality of the adjunction unit, and naturality of the Kummer boundary identify $x^{-1}b_T$ with $b_\Omega$. The latter is an isomorphism by the decomposition clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], applied only to the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and to this same $B$ and $N$. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies the stalks of each cohomology sheaf of $\operatorname{Cone}(b_T)$ with those of $\operatorname{Cone}(b_\Omega)$; they vanish. Conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to $0\to\mathcal H^j\operatorname{Cone}(b_T)$, makes each such sheaf zero. Thus $b_T$ is an isomorphism over arbitrary $T$. Define $t_T=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_T^{-1}$. This is the evaluated tower trace because it uses the same two splitting components. Moreover geometric-point exchange carries $t_T$ to $t_\Omega$: it carries the components of $b_T$, hence its inverse and second projection, to those over $\Omega$. This proves the needed trace comparison without applying a Noetherian-base theorem to $T$.

Now put $T=P$ and take either $r=p_i:W\to P$. Let $\delta_B:R\Delta_*B_P\to B_W(1)[2]$ be its supported diagonal Kummer map and $u_\Delta:B_W\to R\Delta_*B_P$ the restriction unit. The arbitrary-base statement [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] gives $\delta_Bu_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$ and Cartier-preserving base-change compatibility, including scalar extension to $B$. Write $\beta_i=Rp_{i*}\delta_B\circ\alpha_i$ with $\alpha_i:B_P\simeq Rp_{i*}R\Delta_*B_P$. The composite-adjunction unit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives $\alpha_i=Rp_{i*}u_\Delta\circ\eta_{p_i}$ since $p_i\Delta=1$. Hence $\beta_i=Rp_{i*}(\delta_Bu_\Delta)\circ\eta_{p_i}$.

For a geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$, the fibre $F=W\times_{P,p_i}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$, and the pullback $D_x$ of $\Delta$ is its single rational point. If that point has coordinates $[a_0:a_1]$, its equation is $a_0y_1-a_1y_0$ up to sign. Since one $a_j$ is nonzero, this is a Cartier divisor, including at infinity; dividing by $y_j$ on the standard charts shows that its divisor line bundle has the transition functions of $\mathcal O_F(1)$. Thus the supported-class base-change hypothesis holds. Proper exchange [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring], natural in the class, takes $x^{-1}\beta_i$ to the adjoint of $c_1(\mathcal O_F(D_x))=c_1(\mathcal O_F(1))$, namely $h_\Omega$. This also fixes the source identification: the exchange defined in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], as the counit mate, satisfies $\operatorname{Ex}\circ x^{-1}\eta_{p_i}=\eta_r$ for $r:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. More explicitly, write $f=p_i$, $v:F\to W$, $r:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $L=B_P$, and $\theta:r^{-1}x^{-1}\simeq v^{-1}f^{-1}$. The mate formula and naturality of $\eta_r$ give
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{f^{-1}L}\circ x^{-1}\eta_{f,L}=Rr_*\bigl(v^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,f^{-1}L}\circ\theta_{Rf_*f^{-1}L}\circ r^{-1}x^{-1}\eta_{f,L}\bigr)\circ\eta_{r,x^{-1}L}.$$
Naturality of $\theta$ replaces the expression in parentheses by $v^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,f^{-1}L}\circ f^{-1}\eta_{f,L})\circ\theta_L=\theta_L$. The adjunction triangle makes the parenthesized composite the identity after the indicated pullback identification, leaving $\eta_{r,x^{-1}L}$. Consequently the geometric pullback of $t_P\beta_i$ equals $t_\Omega h_\Omega=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_\Omega^{-1}b_\Omega\iota_2=1$.

Degree-zero full faithfulness [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] writes $t_P\beta_i$ as a sheaf endomorphism $f_i$ of $B_P$. The image $I$ of $f_i-1$ has zero geometric stalks by exactness [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. Conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to $0\to I$ gives $I=0$, so $f_i=1$. Transporting by $\nu_P^*$ proves $(c_i)_n=1$ for both $i$. Step 2 gives $c_1=c_2=1$. The finite projective-line input was used only over geometric fields, not over the arbitrary base $S$; no finite-type assumption on $S$ or flatness of a coefficient quotient was used.

proof.text:
*First triangle, integrating along $p_1$.* Expand $F\eta_M$ using its definition, replace $qp_2$ by $qp_1$, and then apply $\varepsilon_{FM}$. With the canonical direct-image composition maps and the projection formula of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] this gives
$$FM=R(qp_1)_{*,\bullet}\Delta_*M\longrightarrow R(qp_1)_{*,\bullet}p_1^*M(1)[2]\simeq F\bigl(M\otimes^LRp_{1*,\bullet}A_W(1)[2]\bigr)\xrightarrow{F(1_M\otimes t_1)}FM.$$
Here $t_1$ is the base-changed trace identified in step 1. The first arrow is $\delta_\bullet\otimes p_1^*M$. Naturality of the projection comparison identifies its pushforward along $p_1$, including the source identification $\Delta^*p_1^*M=M$, with $1_M\otimes Rp_{1*,\bullet}\delta_\bullet$. The exchange and projection reordering is the equality in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the tower-topos ring object $A_\bullet$; [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] supplies the specified composition comparisons on this model. Thus the entire composite is $F(1_M\otimes c_1)=1_{FM}$ by step 3, rather than merely a map which becomes an identity on evaluation.

proof.text: *Second triangle, integrating along $p_2$.* Put $M=GK$. On $W$ both $p_1^*M$ and $p_2^*M$ equal $(qp_1)^*K(1)[2]$, since $qp_1=qp_2$ and the twist pulls back from $S$. Factor $p_2^*M$ out of $Rp_{2*,\bullet}(A_W\otimes^Lp_2^*M)(1)[2]$ by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The arrow induced by $\delta_\bullet$ becomes $1_M\otimes Rp_{2*,\bullet}\delta_\bullet$, with source $M\otimes A_P$. Under proper exchange, $G\varepsilon_K$ contracts the remaining factor $Rp_{2*,\bullet}A_W(1)[2]$ by $t_2$, by step 1. The exchange/projection compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the same tower ringed topos verifies these are the canonical maps. Hence $G\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}=1_{GK}\otimes c_2=1_{GK}$. Only even shifts have been moved past tensor factors, so their Koszul signs are $(-1)^{2j}=1$. The interchange of the two unshifted twist lines is also the identity: locally choose a generator $e$; the symmetry sends $ae\otimes be$ to $be\otimes ae=ab(e\otimes e)$ over the commutative coefficient ring. These local equalities give the stated canonical symmetry globally.

source.place: Reduction of the triangle identities: second triangle

proof.text: *Adjunction from the two triangles.* For a tower map $u:FM\to K$ define $\Phi(u)=G(u)\circ\eta_M$, and for $v:M\to GK$ define $\Psi(v)=\varepsilon_K\circ F(v)$. Naturality and step 4 give $\Psi\Phi(u)=u\circ\varepsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M=u$. Naturality and step 5 give $\Phi\Psi(v)=G\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}\circ v=v$. These operations are natural in $M,K$, so they are the Hom bijection exhibiting $F\dashv G$ with the specified unit and counit.

*Evaluation and restriction.* For each $n\geq1$, exact evaluation sends $A_ ullet$ to $(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, sends $\delta_ ullet$ to the finite supported diagonal class, and sends the splitting inverse followed by its second projection to the finite trace, by [det-sp-tower-classes]. The specified tensor, direct-image, exchange and projection comparisons evaluate to their finite comparisons by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; shifts and inverse image are termwise. Substituting these in the displayed formulas gives the finite diagonal-defined unit and splitting-trace-defined counit with the actual coefficients $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Here is an explicit verification that these maps form the finite adjunction on bounded-below etale-origin levels. Given a bounded-below complex $L$ of etale $B$-module sheaves on a scheme $T$, put $
u_T^*L$ at level $n$ and the zero complex at every other level, with every transition zero. This is a bounded-below complex of towers by the componentwise definition [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], and is in $\mathscr C^+(T)$. Denote its derived object by $J_nL$. Write $F_n=Rq_{*,B}$ and $G_n=q^{-1}(-)(1)[2]$ on the finite etale categories. Evaluate the first tower triangle of Step 4 on $J_nM$, for arbitrary $M\in D^+(P_{\mathrm{et}},B)$: the specified comparisons give
$$
u_S^* igl(\varepsilon_{n,F_nM}\circ F_n(\eta_{n,M}) igr)=1_{
u_S^*F_nM}.$$
Evaluate the second tower triangle of Step 5 on $J_nK$, for arbitrary $K\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},B)$: they give
$$
u_P^* igl(G_n(\varepsilon_{n,K})\circ\eta_{n,G_nK} igr)=1_{
u_P^*G_nK}.$$
Full faithfulness [sk-prop-sf-comparison] removes $
u^*$ from both equalities. Thus the finite maps satisfy both triangles for every finite bounded-below input. Explicitly the inverse Hom operations are $u\mapsto G_n(u)\eta_{n,M}$ and $v\mapsto\varepsilon_{n,K}F_n(v)$, whose composites are $u\varepsilon_{n,F_nM}F_n\eta_{n,M}=u$ and $G_n\varepsilon_{n,K}\eta_{n,G_nK}v=v$. This proves the finite adjunction over the arbitrary base using the evaluated maps. To see that the full uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories lie in $\mathscr C^+$, use [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] locally on affine $U$ and [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] with [sk-prop-sf-comparison]: the classical cohomology condition is local, so the bounded-below equivalence gives a global etale-origin witness for each bounded constructible level. Uniform cohomological bounds give a bounded-below tower because tower cohomology and vanishing are levelwise [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Finally [sk-lem-sp-tower-bound], with $f=q$, preserves uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers under $F$; for $G$ the bounds can be checked locally over each affine open $U\subseteq S$, where both $U$ and $\mathbf P^1_U$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. With $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$, the constructible comparison [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] gives a bounded constructible etale representative $L_n$ of $K_n|_U$. The same fixed Tor interval $[a,b]$ holds for $L_n$ by [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]. Choose its flat representative supported in $[a,b]$ using [lem-sf-etale-flat-model]. A bounded complex of flat sheaves is K-flat: tensoring each flat term with an acyclic complex is acyclic, and the finite filtration by shifted terms gives the assertion for the complex. The termwise pullback along $q$ is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], and remains supported in $[a,b]$. Tensor with the locally free rank-one twist and shift by $[2]$ gives a flat complex supported in $[a-2,b-2]$; its tensor with any degree-zero test sheaf has no other terms, so this is its Tor interval. Transfer the interval back to the pro-etale site by [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]. Exact inverse image preserves the cohomological interval, and inverse-image strata and their pulled-back finite constant trivializations show constructibility. These bounds hold for every $n$ and every $U$; vanishing is local, so they hold globally, with the shift moving both bounds by $-2$. Hence both functors preserve the full tower subcategories [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and the same Hom bijection restricts to them.
